title: Metastable MnGe2 Thin Films Grown on MnO(001) Substrates by Magnetron-Sputtering Technique
content: Efficient spin injection into semiconductors has sparked interest in synthesizing diluted magnetic semiconductors (DMS) obtained by substituting 3d transition metal atoms, such as Mn, Co, Fe, Cr, or Ni, into nonmagnetic semiconductors. Mn-doped Ge (Ge1−xMnx) offers a direct route for integrating magnetism with the existing silicon technology; however, DMS have a very low Curie temperature (TC) [1]. Self-organized Ge1−xMnx nanocolumns with an average diameter of 3 nm and spacing of 10 nm were observed. Their composition is close to MnGe2, and magnetic measurements showed a TC > 400 K [2]. The metastable phase MnGe2 has a C16-type structure (y = 0.33, tetragonal I4/mcm symmetry) with lattice parameters a = 5.96 Å and c = 5.03 Å. The non-primitive unit cell contains 12 atoms, four Mn in positions 4(a) and eight Ge in positions 8(h) [3].
